 Chef who worked with Marco Pierre White takes over village pub

 The couple met two-and-a-bit years ago and have numerous experience in the hospitality (Image: NQ) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 An Oxfordshire chef who began his career working with Marco Pierre White has taken over a village pub with ambitions of creating a destination dining venue.
 Dan Roth of King Sutton is the new co-owner and head chef at The Stag in Flackwell Heath, Buckinghamshire, with his girlfriend, Sophie Bartlett, 25.
 The 30-year-old brings with him more than 14 years of hospitality experience and a track record of helping transform pubs into successful businesses.
 Mr Roth's journey started when he was just 16 years old, working as a commis chef for a company owned by Marco Pierre White.
 READ MORE: King Charles 'tried to get away from' rapist Russell Brand 
 The pub is based along Heath End Road (Image: NQ) 
 During his early years in the kitchen, he gained valuable experience working alongside one of Britain's most recognisable chefs.
 He said: “I got the pleasure of working with Marco at times. You definitely knew when he was there."
 The Oxfordshire connection continued when Mr Roth joined The White Horse in King Sutton, near Banbury, as a teenager.
 The pub had recently been taken over by a young couple who transformed its fortunes, winning awards and building a reputation for high-quality food.
 Watching that success unfold left a lasting impression, as Mr Roth said: "That was what hooked me.
 READ MORE: Boris Johnson reveals his ancestor was a slave as he blasts cash demands 
 Dan Roth and Sophie Bartlett have taken over the Stag in Flackwell Heath (Image: NQ) 
 “Seeing young owners come into a pub that needed some love and completely turn it around made me think, one day I'd love to do that myself."
 Over the following decade, he worked across several well-known venues, eventually becoming head chef at the Belgian Arms in Holyport.
 There, he helped guide the kitchen to an AA Rosette, inclusion in the Good Food Guide and recognition among the UK's leading gastropubs.
 He later played a key role in reopening The Beehive in White Waltham as a village pub after it had previously operated as a curry house.
 Those experiences, he says, have prepared him for his biggest challenge yet.
 READ MORE: Singer's entire UK tour CANCELLED after comments on Russell Brand 
 The Stag has been based in Flackwell Heath since the 1800s (Image: NQ) 
 The Stag has seen several operators come and go in recent years, but Mr Roth believes the lessons learned throughout his career can help turn the business into a lasting success.
 His food philosophy remains rooted in traditional pub cooking, as he added: “I've always been a pub chef. I've never wanted to make food overly complicated.
 "If someone orders a cottage pie, they should get a cottage pie, but hopefully it's the best one they've ever eaten."
 While awards may come later, Mr Roth insists the immediate focus is winning over local customers.
 He concluded: “We want to get the community behind us first. If we can make the locals proud of The Stag again, then we'll know we're doing something right."
